description: Paired conformance vectors: same two-action session (benign ls, malicious curl|bash) signed by two different key deployment models. Variant A uses an external sidecar key (private key not published); Variant B uses a deterministic in-process key. Each variant records two independent verdicts: chain integrity (cryptographic) and behavior evidence (semantic).

chain_integrity.description: Cryptographic verdict: does the Ed25519 signature over the JCS-canonicalized receipt verify against the published public key?

behavior_evidence.description: Semantic verdict: did the verifier observe and act on malicious behavior? This verdict is attested by the signed receipt but cannot be independently verified by a third party without re-running the verifier.

pdr_crosswalk_notes: These vectors complement Providex-AI/rootsign PDR receipts (Zenodo DOI 10.5281/zenodo.19984948). CCS receipts provide the cryptographic chain-integrity layer; PDR evidence-lineage provides the behavioral provenance layer. A future crosswalk document will map CCS receipt fields to PDR evidence-lineage fields.
